text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Consecrate to me every firstborn. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal."
Then Moses said to the people, "Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, for the LORD brought you out of it with a mighty hand. No leavened bread is to be eaten.
Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.

versions.text: Today, in the month of Abib, you are going out.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew places the time-marker "in the month of Abib" after the main clause; keeping that order reads more smoothly aloud than interrupting the sentence. A footnote explaining that Abib is the first month of the year (roughly March–April), later called Nisan, would help hearers unfamiliar with the name.

text: When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you are to keep this observance in this month.
For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a festival to the LORD.
Unleavened bread is to be eaten throughout the seven days; no leavened bread is to be seen among you, and no yeast is to be seen anywhere within your borders.
On that day you shall tell your son, 'This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.'
It shall be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder between your eyes, so that the law of the LORD may be on your lips; for with a mighty hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
You shall keep this statute at its appointed time, year after year.
"When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as he swore to you and to your fathers,
you shall give over to the LORD the first offspring of every womb. Every firstborn male of your livestock belongs to the LORD.
Every firstborn donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. And every firstborn among your sons you shall redeem.
When your son asks you in time to come, 'What does this mean?' you shall tell him, 'With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of humans and the firstborn of animals. That is why I sacrifice to the LORD every firstborn male, and why I redeem every firstborn of my sons.'
It shall be a sign on your hand and a symbol between your eyes that with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.

versions.text: It shall be a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead that with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew phrase is identical to the one in verse 9 (בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ, "between your eyes"), which this translation renders literally there. Rendering it "on your forehead" here creates an inconsistency between two parallel verses in the same chapter and obscures the verbal link.

text: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, "If they face war, they may change their minds and return to Egypt."
So God led the people around by the wilderness road toward the Red Sea. The Israelites went up out of Egypt in battle array.

versions.text: So God led the people around by the desert road toward the Red Sea. The Israelites went up out of Egypt in battle array.
versions.explanation: The same Hebrew word (מִדְבָּר) is rendered "wilderness" in verse 20 but "desert" here; using one term consistently within the chapter aids oral comprehension. A footnote noting that the Hebrew reads "Sea of Reeds" could also be helpful.

text: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, because Joseph had made the Israelites swear a solemn oath, saying, "God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up with you from here."
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
By day the LORD went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to guide them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day and by night.

versions.text: By day the LORD went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to guide them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day or by night.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has "day and night" (יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה), stressing continuous travel; "day or by night" weakens this to an alternative.

text: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night ever left its place in front of the people.
